title: CVS Pharmacies Nationwide Now Fill Prescriptions for Dogs and Cats
excerpt: The pharmacy giant has expanded into pet healthcare, allowing owners to fill veterinary prescriptions at approximately 9,000 locations across the United States — with delivery, automatic refills, and app management included.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • CVS now fills pet prescriptions at approximately 9,000 locations across the U.S.
  • Available medications include antibiotics, insulin, and pain relievers for pets.
  • Pet owners can manage prescriptions via the CVS Health app and website.
  • The U.S. pet industry reached $158 billion in 2025, with rising costs affecting medication access.
  • CVS aims to provide convenience and competitive pricing for pet medications.

  • CVS Health announced on July 21, 2026 that all approximately 9,000 CVS Pharmacy locations now dispense prescription medications for dogs and cats.
  • Available pet medications include antibiotics, allergy treatments, flea and tick control, insulin, and pain relievers, with automatic refill and delivery options.
  • Pet owners can manage prescriptions through the CVS Health app and CVS.com, with electronic prescribing capabilities planned for later this year.
  • The U.S. pet industry reached $158 billion in spending in 2025, and about 25% of pet owners have skipped or delayed medications due to cost.

CVS Enters the Pet Pharmacy Business

CVS Health has made its biggest push into pet healthcare, announcing on July 21 that all of its approximately 9,000 pharmacy locations across the United States will now fill prescription medications for dogs and cats. The move positions the nation's largest pharmacy chain as a direct competitor to veterinary clinics and online pet pharmacies.

The available medications cover routine and chronic pet health needs: antibiotics, allergy treatments, flea and tick control products, insulin for diabetic pets, and pain relievers. Pet owners can bring a written prescription from their veterinarian or have the vet contact the pharmacy directly.

> **"pet industry expenditures reached $158 billion in 2025 — a 3.7% increase — and are projected to climb to $165 billion in 2026."**

"With the addition of pet medication dispensing, CVS Pharmacy can now serve every member of the family."

— Sid Tenneti, Senior Vice President and Interim President, Pharmacy and Consumer Wellness, CVS Health

Amy Thibault, a CVS spokesperson, told USA TODAY that pet medication prices at CVS are comparable to what owners would pay at a veterinarian's office. The differentiator lies in convenience: CVS offers the same pharmacy services for pet prescriptions that human patients already use, including automatic refills, prescription syncing, and home delivery where eligible.

Digital Integration and Future Plans

Pet owners can add their animals to their CVS.com profiles and manage prescriptions through the CVS Health app, tracking refills and delivery alongside their own medications. Electronic prescribing — allowing veterinarians to send prescriptions digitally to CVS — will be added in the coming months, eliminating the need for paper prescriptions.

Beyond prescriptions, CVS has expanded its in-store pet product offerings through its Pet Central brand, which includes grooming tools, wellness accessories, toys, and training pads. National brands like Milk-Bone, Greenies, and Temptations have also been added to shelves, with new items expected in September.

A $158 Billion Industry Under Pressure

CVS's timing reflects broader trends in the American pet industry. According to the American Pet Products Association, U.S. pet industry expenditures reached $158 billion in 2025 — a 3.7% increase — and are projected to climb to $165 billion in 2026. Pet ownership remained stable at 95 million households, with dog ownership at 53% of households (71 million homes) and cat ownership at 39% (53 million).

Pet Prescription Management Made Easy
›Manage pet prescriptions through CVS Health app.
›Automatic refills and delivery options available.
›Electronic prescribing to be introduced soon.
›Convenience for busy pet owners.

But veterinary costs remain a pressure point. A GoodRx study from October 2025 found that about 25% of pet owners have skipped, delayed, or changed a pet's medication due to cost. Among dog owners, 32% spend between $200 and $499 annually on prescriptions alone. For a chain with CVS's scale, these numbers represent a substantial market opportunity.

What It Means for Diaspora Pet Owners

Pet ownership among Indian Americans has grown steadily, particularly among younger members of the diaspora. Research from Mars Petcare found that two-thirds of Gen Z and Millennial pet parents consider their pet the most important thing in their lives — a sentiment reflected in Indian American households where dogs and cats are increasingly treated as family.

For busy diaspora families, filling a pet prescription at the same pharmacy where they pick up their own medications is a practical convenience. The app-based management and delivery options appeal to digitally savvy households, and transparent retail pricing may ease the sticker shock of U.S. veterinary costs for newer immigrants.

What's Next

CVS has not disclosed whether it plans to expand its pet medication range or integrate with pet insurance providers. The key question is whether the move will prompt competitors like Walgreens to follow suit, reshaping a market long split between veterinary clinics and online retailers. For 95 million American pet-owning households facing rising costs, more options at the pharmacy counter are welcome news.
